name: fact-currency-check
what_it_does: Checks whether a claim, version number, citation or referenced issue is still true today, not just true when it was written.
what_you_say: is this still true? or "check these claims before we act on them"
what_you_get: Each claim marked current, stale, or not checkable, with the source it was checked against.
on_your_computer: Looks things up online, and may run the software a claim is about. Changes nothing.

name: overengineering-review
what_it_does: Reads a change or a whole project and lists code that could be removed: options nobody sets, layers with one user, hand-made copies of built-in functions.
what_you_say: is this over-engineered? or "what can we delete?"
what_you_get: One line per finding with the code quoted and the search that backs it. It removes nothing.
on_your_computer: Reads your code and runs searches that only look, such as `git grep`. Changes nothing.

name: review-pair
what_it_does: Has a second, separate reviewer judge one proposed change against its stated goal before the change is made.
what_you_get: A written verdict of pass or fail with reasons. On a pass, the change is applied.
on_your_computer: Starts a second Claude helper, runs a small checking script on its answer, and on a pass applies the reviewed change to your files.

name: security-audit
what_it_does: A full security audit of a codebase from its source: finds weaknesses, tries to reproduce them safely, and writes a findings report. It is a large third-party skill from Cloudflare, included unchanged.
what_you_say: run a full security audit of this repo
what_you_get: For a question, advice in the conversation. For a full audit, a folder of reports including a list of findings.
on_your_computer: For a full audit it creates a reports folder in your home directory, starts several helper agents up to a limit it sets at the start, and may build and run the code being audited inside a sandbox, a restricted area with no internet. Needs Node.

name: security-checklist
what_it_does: A pass or fail security checklist for one change or one file before it ships: secrets, input handling, sign-in, data exposure, dependencies, cloud settings.
what_you_get: A checklist with pass, fail or not checkable per item, and proposed fixes it does not carry out.
on_your_computer: Reads the code you point at and may run a dependency check (`npm audit`, `pip-audit`), which contacts the package registry. Changes nothing.

name: site-review
what_it_does: Scores a live website for speed, accessibility and broken links, then fixes problems on a separate branch, so your main files stay as they were until you accept the fixes.
what_you_get: A score table, the list of broken links, screenshots, and proposed fixes.
on_your_computer: Downloads two website-checking tools (Lighthouse and linkinator) on first use, runs a hidden Chrome window against the live site, follows its links, writes report files, and edits your site's files on a separate branch. Needs Node.

name: smoke-gate
what_it_does: Builds a quick "is it actually up?" check for something you deployed, and proves the check can fail before trusting it.
what_you_say: make a smoke test for this deploy
what_you_get: A small script in your project that checks your site or service, a log of each run, and one screenshot.
on_your_computer: Writes a script into your project, makes network requests to the address you name, and can be set up to stop Claude Code from finishing a turn while the check fails. Needs Python, PyYAML and `curl`.

name: pre-delivery-verifier
what_it_does: Checks a finished piece of work against its acceptance list by running the real checks, before you are told it is done.
what_you_say: verify this before you hand it over
what_you_get: A report of each check run, its actual output, and whether the work passed.
on_your_computer: Runs your own build, tests or checkers. It is set up so it cannot change files.

name: silent-failure-hunter
what_it_does: Reads code for failures that would happen quietly: errors that are caught and ignored, fallbacks that hide a real problem.
what_you_say: hunt for silent failures in this module
what_you_get: A list of findings with file and line. It fixes nothing.
on_your_computer: Reads your code. Runs nothing and changes nothing.
